# SB-1037 - Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Hazard description
- Background: Routine abrasive blasting in the heat treat area produces dust containing metallic and nonmetallic particulates. These particulates can become airborne during operation of the Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03), during loading and unloading, and during media replenishment. Airborne dust presents inhalation and visibility hazards for operators and adjacent personnel, increases maintenance burdens on downstream filtration systems, and can deposit on parts, affecting quality.
- Hazard mechanism: The blasting process fractures shot media and abraded material from workpieces, creating respirable and nonrespirable fractions. Agitation during top-up and cabinet access disturbs settled material, increasing short duration dust emissions. Accumulation of dust in local work zones can result in elevated exposures during routine tasks that are not directly part of blasting.
- Consequences: Potential outcomes include operator respiratory irritation, potential exacerbation of chronic respiratory conditions for exposed personnel, nonconformance due to particulate contamination of heat-treated parts, and increased frequency of unplanned maintenance activities related to dust ingress in ancillary equipment.

Affected equipment
- Primary: Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03).
- Secondary: Adjacent conveyors and workstations on line P3-L4, local ventilation ductwork that serves EQ-P3-L4-SB03, and nearby work areas where settled dust may re-enter the breathing zone during normal operations.
- Personnel: Operators assigned to EQ-P3-L4-SB03, maintenance personnel performing cabinet access or media top-up, and housekeeping staff conducting cleaning in the immediate area.

Required controls
The following controls are mandatory for operations involving EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Controls are ordered by preferred hierarchy and include administrative steps to maintain engineering controls.

Engineering controls
- Maintain and verify containment integrity of EQ-P3-L4-SB03 before each shift. Confirm door gaskets, viewing windows, and access panels seat properly to prevent fugitive dust escape.
- Confirm local exhaust ventilation that serves EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is operational and set to the design airflow. If the system shows reduced performance, remove equipment from service and tag out until corrected.
- Use enclosed transfer procedures for shot media top-up to minimize agitation of settled dust. When refilling media reservoirs or hoppers, align transfer funnels and use sealed transfer pans provided for EQ-P3-L4-SB03.

Work practices and administrative controls
- The shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 48 hours. Media top-up actions must be scheduled to respect this interval and to coordinate with ventilation verification activities described above.
- Implement a pre-top-up checklist that includes verification of ventilation flow, availability of sealed transfer equipment, and presence of required personal protective equipment.
- Limit the number of personnel in the immediate cabinet area during top-up and loading/unloading to those required to perform the task.
- Keep a log of all top-up events, maintenance entries, and observed dust releases. Use the log to inform frequency adjustments and to support corrective actions.
- Coordinate work with adjacent line P3-L4 teams to prevent concurrent operations that could elevate local dust levels.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
- Require respiratory protection when personnel are performing tasks where engineering controls cannot fully prevent exposure during top-up, access, or when visible dust is present. Respiratory protection must be selected per the site respiratory protection program and documented on the pre-top-up checklist.
- Use eye protection and appropriate protective clothing as defined in plant standard PPE procedures for blasting areas.

Step rationale and examples
- Rationale for containment and ventilation: Preventing dust from leaving the cabinet is the most effective way to reduce exposure and downstream contamination. Ensuring gaskets and access panels seal reduces the need for escalated PPE and limits housekeeping burdens.
- Rationale for the top-up interval: Adhering to the shot media top-up interval for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is intended to minimize disturbance frequency of settled media and to provide predictable scheduling for ventilation verification and personnel assignment. Predictable top-up scheduling reduces the likelihood of uncoordinated activities that could cause short-term spikes in airborne dust.
- Example procedure: Prior to initiating a top-up, the operator completes the pre-top-up checklist, notifies adjacent workstations on line P3-L4, confirms the sealed transfer funnel is engaged, and dons required PPE. After transfer completion, the operator waits for ventilation verification confirmation before opening the cabinet for inspection.

Records to keep
- Top-up log: Record each top-up event for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 with the following entries: operator name, start and end of transfer activity, verification status of ventilation, and any deviations or observed dust escape. Retain the top-up log in the cabinet control binder.
- Maintenance and verification records: Document all containment inspections, gasket replacements, and ventilation performance verifications in the equipment maintenance record for EQ-P3-L4-SB03.
- Incident reports: For any observed uncontrolled dust release, complete an incident report and submit to P3 safety management. Include mitigation actions taken and follow-up measures.
- Training records: Maintain training records demonstrating that personnel assigned to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 have been trained on this bulletin and on the pre-top-up checklist.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-026
- SB-1038
- SOP-P3-L4-03

Effective date
- Effective date: Rev E

Notes
- This safety bulletin will be reviewed in coordination with referenced documents ECN-2026-026, SB-1038, and SOP-P3-L4-03 during the next scheduled document review cycle. Any deviations from the controls specified here require approval from P3 safety management and documentation in the EQ-P3-L4-SB03 maintenance record.
